name: Ember of Rebellion

stars.name: Fracture
stars.notes: A stable yellow star whose name reflects not its nature but the system's: a colony that turned on itself. Before the civil war, the star was called 'Prosperity.' No one uses that name anymore.

planets.name: Crucible
planets.notes: Scorched inner rock. The Loyalist faction uses its shadow for fleet staging—ships powered down in the star's glare are nearly invisible to rebel sensors.

planets.name: Kindred
planets.notes: The system's primary world and the heart of the civil war. A temperate, populous planet of 8 million, now divided between the Loyalist-held coastal cities and the Reformist-held interior. The front line cuts through the main continent like a wound.

planets.name: Splinter
planets.notes: A cold, marginal colony world of 400,000 that declared for the Reformists early in the war. Its remote location and rugged terrain make it an ideal rebel logistics hub, though Loyalist raids on supply convoys are increasing.

planets.name: The Divide
planets.notes: Airless world that serves as the de facto boundary between Loyalist and Reformist-controlled space. Both sides maintain observation posts on its moons, watching each other across the void.

planets.name: Old Plenty
planets.notes: Named during the prosperous years, this banded giant's fuel-harvesting operations are contested. Loyalists control the primary extraction platforms; Reformists raid them regularly, creating a fuel shortage that constrains both sides.

planets.name: Remnant
planets.notes: Frozen outer world. Reformist intelligence has established a covert communications hub in its subsurface ice caves, relaying encrypted messages to sympathizers in neighboring systems.

planets.name: Ash
planets.notes: The system's outermost body, small and dark. Named by war-weary colonists who see in it the future of everything they built.

anomalies.name: The Rift
anomalies.notes: The front line on Kindred's surface is saturated with electronic warfare emissions from both sides. A band approximately 200 kilometers wide along the main continental divide is a communications dead zone—signals are jammed, spoofed, or intercepted within seconds.

anomalies.name: Loyalty's Price
anomalies.notes: Wreckage of the colonial defense fleet, which split along factional lines during the first week of the civil war. The resulting orbital battle destroyed eleven ships and created a debris hazard that persists in low orbit.

asteroid_belts.name: Prosperity Belt
asteroid_belts.notes: Named during better times, this belt's mining operations have been disrupted by the war. Both factions raid each other's mining convoys, and independent miners have largely fled the system.

stations.name: Loyalist High Command
stations.location: High orbit around Kindred, above coastal cities
stations.notes: The Loyalist faction's military and political headquarters. Commands the larger fleet but faces increasing logistical strain as the war drags on and trade partners distance themselves from the conflict.

stations.name: Free Kindred Station
stations.notes: The Reformist faction's primary orbital facility. Smaller and less well-equipped than the Loyalist station, but sustained by popular support and a network of external sympathizers who funnel supplies through back channels.

stations.name: Neutral Harbor
stations.notes: A humanitarian station operated by the Meridian Aid Compact, processing refugees fleeing the front lines on Kindred. Both factions have agreed to respect its neutrality—so far.

faction_control.primary: Civil war — Kindred Loyalist Government / Reformist Liberation Front
faction_control.notes: What began as a political dispute over colonial governance in 2721 has escalated into a full civil war. The Loyalists hold the cities, the fleet, and the economic infrastructure; the Reformists hold the hinterlands, popular support, and a cause. Neither side can win decisively. The war has displaced 1.2 million people and killed approximately 40,000.

history: The Prosperity System, as it was known, was a model colony for over a century—well-governed, economically productive, socially cohesive. The rot began in the 2710s when the colonial governor's family consolidated power, redirecting public resources to cronies and suppressing dissent.

The Reformist Liberation Front formed in 2719 as a political movement demanding democratic reforms. When the governor responded with mass arrests in 2721, the movement militarized. The colonial defense fleet split—roughly 60% Loyalist, 40% Reformist—and the orbital battle that followed destroyed eleven ships and marked the point of no return.

Five years of civil war have transformed a prosperous colony into a humanitarian catastrophe. The Loyalist government maintains international recognition but diminishing legitimacy. The Reformists control territory but lack the industrial capacity for a sustained campaign. External powers supply both sides through proxies, prolonging the conflict. The Meridian Aid Compact's humanitarian station processes an average of 200 refugees per week.
description: Ember of Rebellion is a system consuming itself. Seven worlds orbit a yellow star that was once called Prosperity, and the bitter irony of that name hangs over everything. Kindred, the primary world, is split by a front line that cuts across its largest continent—Loyalist coastal cities on one side, Reformist-held farmland and mountains on the other. Splinter, the smaller colony, has thrown in with the Reformists and serves as their logistical backbone. Between them, the space is contested, mined, and dangerous.

The civil war is in its fifth year, and exhaustion is setting in without bringing resolution. The Loyalists have the ships and the cities but face economic collapse as trade partners distance themselves from a government increasingly seen as authoritarian. The Reformists have popular support and territorial depth but lack the industrial capacity to build warships or heavy weapons. The front line on Kindred has barely moved in two years. Both sides raid each other's supply lines. Both sides commit atrocities they justify as necessities. The humanitarian station at Neutral Harbor fills with refugees who have lost everything.

For outsiders, the Ember offers the grim opportunities of any civil war. Both factions need weapons, supplies, and mercenaries. Intelligence services from neighboring systems cultivate assets on both sides, positioning for influence in whatever government emerges from the ashes. War correspondents document the conflict for audiences who express concern and change nothing. And in the refugee camps of Neutral Harbor, aid workers confront the human cost of a war that no one seems able to end.
